title: Bits, Bytes, and Number Bases

title: Multiplexers and Decoders
summary: A multiplexer selects one of several inputs to pass through based on a control signal; a decoder does the reverse, activating exactly one output line based on a binary input — two small, reusable circuits that show up everywhere in a real CPU.

title: Latches and Flip-Flops

title: Registers
summary: A group of flip-flops, one per bit, clocked together — a single circuit that holds an entire word of state at once, and the smallest unit of storage a CPU actually reads from and writes to directly.

title: Finite State Machines: Design and Analysis

title: From Flip-Flops to a Register File
